correctness.rationale: The four triangles are exactly the first-coordinate triples; the reversal edges uniquely identify which triangle each vertex pairs with. An automorphism is consequently determined by permuting the four triangles, and every such permutation acts. Independent subsets are partial functions without fixed points or mutual reversals. In the barycentric subdivision the distinct cardinalities in any one flag force identifications within a closed simplex to fix its supporting vertices and coefficients, so closed cells embed in the orbit space. All facets have distinct omitted ranks, giving the stated regular CW collapse test. I independently generated faces and flags by combinations and strict submask recursion and recovered (12,48,72,30) source faces, 3342 flags and (11,42,63,30) orbit cells. Replaying the actual frozen collapse_pairs.json against rebuilt incidence verified all sixty free-face pairs, with each higher cell maximal on removal, and the resulting closure has (6,12,8) cells. Each edge has two incident triangles and each vertex has a connected 2-regular link with multiplicities; the core is connected and has Euler characteristic two. This proves the closed PL sphere core and the simple-homotopy claim by the regular cellular collapses. The core is a regular triangular cellulation with parallel edges (e.g. two between vertices 1 and 6 under frozen indexing), not an abstract simplicial complex without subdivision; its barycentric subdivision is a combinatorial two-sphere in the strict simplicial sense.
residual_risks: The quotient collapses onto the indicated sphere and is not asserted to be homeomorphic to it. Use the regular CW or subdivided interpretation of the spherical core, not a claim that its unsubdivided incidence is an abstract simplicial complex.

originality.rationale: A distinct indexed record, cd45e6d28233, demonstrably covers the same integral sphere claim and the same stronger existence of a sixty-step elementary collapse onto a PL sphere. Its stated core-recognition proof uses attaching words rather than surface links; however I checked its actual certificate in a common orbit indexing, and its residual core itself satisfies the same closed-surface criterion. Its pair sequence really is different, but gives equivalent scientific coverage, not a new quotient or stronger structural conclusion. Both records have publication date 2026-11-22 UTC; within-day order and priority are not established, and this coverage finding is not a claim about who was first.
residual_risks: There is no priority inference from identical UTC publication dates. A second cited November 8 rational-homology record, 1ca9caa90c0c, was unavailable in the local mirror; that limitation is not the basis of the negative decision. This is a scoped result comparison, not a general historical-priority conclusion.

value.rationale: The original integral upgrade over rational quotient data is a worthwhile exact question. Against the confirmed same-object coverage, however, the only surviving difference is another sixty-pair matching with a different cellulated sphere core and a link-based recognition. The other certificate already leaves a closed PL sphere by the same link test. There is no stronger geometric target, shorter collapse count, minimality claim, extension or independently motivated reason to need this particular set of free-face pairs. This provides corroboration, but not a scientifically distinct finding of the asserted scope.
residual_risks: No claim that an alternative collapse program could not be useful in another context; no such substantive additional application or property is established here.
